- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 3–8%.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 1–4%.
- Model frequently overreacts to sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, forecast may lag; add 1–3 days of lagged sentiment influence.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 5+ days, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–5%.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict in early days (1–7) when sentiment is volatile; dampen first 3–5 days by 2–5%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.44–0.53 peaks, model often fails to capture true breakout; adjust forecast to align with sentiment peak timing.
